title: Ask Claude to use just the facts you give it
summary: Two pretend boats have a pier. One does not. See how Claude deals with a fact that is missing.
where: On Mac or PC open claude.ai in a browser. On iPad open that address in Safari or use Claude by Anthropic. Use an eligible account. You can answer the boat questions on paper, too.

actions.title: Open the tool
actions.do: Type claude.ai in the browser address box. For the iPad app, search the App Store for Claude by Anthropic and open the publisher's listing.
actions.see: Claude opens or asks you to sign in.
actions.stuck: If a search brings up another app, check the address or app publisher before signing in.

actions.title: Start with a blank chat
actions.do: Sign in and start a new conversation. If an account menu offers several spaces, choose one meant for practice.
actions.see: The message box is ready without an earlier question in its history.
actions.stuck: If someone else's work is already on screen, return to the sidebar and start a fresh chat.

actions.title: Give it two clues
actions.do: Send “Blue Ferry boards at Pier 2. Red Ferry boards at Pier 5. Which pier is for Red Ferry? Which is for Gold Ferry? Say unknown if the note leaves it out.”
actions.see: Red uses Pier 5. There is no pier listed for Gold.
actions.stuck: If a pier appears for Gold, ask Claude to quote the line that names it. Check the original two clues yourself.

actions.title: Correct a clue
actions.do: In the same chat, send “Red Ferry now boards at Pier 4. Give the updated answer for Red and Gold.”
actions.see: Red changes to Pier 4. Gold is still unknown.
actions.stuck: If Blue changes too, point out which boat the correction named and ask for a fresh reading.

roles: Explain a fake mail ticket from its text.
Make a note easier for a team to read.
Try a question for a new puzzle game.

title: Open Claude Code and make your first file
summary: Choose a practice folder on your computer. Then find the file Claude creates in that folder.
where: Use Claude Desktop on a Mac or Windows PC with a plan that includes Claude Code. This local route opens a folder on that computer. An iPad cannot pick the computer's folder for you.

actions.title: Get the desktop app
actions.do: Visit claude.com/download and choose the download for your computer. Open the installer. Start Claude from Applications on Mac or Start on Windows and sign in.
actions.see: The Claude desktop window opens under your account.
actions.stuck: If a browser chat opened instead, switch back to the installed Claude app.

actions.title: Choose Code
actions.do: Look near the top of the left sidebar and select Code. If you see pictures with no words, pause the pointer over each one to show its name.
actions.see: You see a place to give Claude Code a job in a project.
actions.stuck: If Code is missing, check your plan and account. The ordinary chat can still explain what a file is.

actions.title: Pick one folder
actions.do: In Documents, make a folder called AI Code Practice using Finder or File Explorer. Under the Code message box choose Local, then the folder control and Open folder. Select AI Code Practice.
actions.see: The project shows the folder you just made.
actions.stuck: If the folder control names Documents, open it and pick AI Code Practice inside it.

actions.title: Make and check a file
actions.do: Send “Create hello.txt. Its only line should be First book test.” If Manual mode asks about this edit, check its file name and approve it. Open hello.txt from the practice folder.
actions.see: The file on your own computer contains exactly First book test.
actions.stuck: If you see only text in the chat, ask Claude to save the file. Check that this session points to your local folder.

roles: Keep a fake mail report in a practice folder.
Write a short guide to a team script.
Make the first real file for a small app.

title: Start Claude Code in a typing window
summary: A terminal lets you type a command and press Enter. Start Claude inside one small folder you can find again.
where: Use Terminal on Mac or PowerShell on Windows with an eligible Claude Code account. This route uses a computer and internet. The separate desktop Code tab is another way to work.
First make AI-Code-Lab inside your home folder using Finder or File Explorer. Read along on iPad while the computer runs the commands.

actions.title: Find the typing window
actions.do: On Mac press Command and Space, type Terminal and press Return. On Windows open Start, type PowerShell and open the regular app.
actions.see: A window with a place to type appears. The cursor waits for your command.
actions.stuck: If you see web results, open the app from your computer's search rather than searching in a browser.

actions.title: Install the command
actions.do: Use Anthropic's setup link to check its current instructions. On Mac the install command is curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash. In Windows PowerShell with WinGet, use winget install Anthropic.ClaudeCode. Press Enter after the command for your computer.
actions.see: The installer finishes and the typing prompt returns.
actions.stuck: If WinGet is missing, follow the Windows choices in the official setup guide. Keep the Mac command for a Mac.

actions.title: Move into the folder
actions.do: Open a fresh terminal window. On either system enter cd
actions.see: /AI-Code-Lab and press Enter. Then enter claude --version and press Enter. The first command changes the folder. The second checks the install.
actions.stuck: A version number appears. Your next commands will run in the practice folder.

actions.title: Start Claude
actions.do: Type claude and press Enter. Finish sign-in if needed. Send “Create greeting.txt containing Hello from my terminal.” Review the file edit if asked, then open the file in the folder.
actions.see: greeting.txt has the line you asked for. You reached the same kind of result as the desktop lesson.
actions.stuck: If you cannot find it, ask which folder Claude is using. Compare that folder with the one in Finder or File Explorer.

roles: Try a reporting command in a safe mail sample folder.
Open a local project of team practice files.
Give a personal app folder to Claude Code.

title: Keep two chats in one Claude Project
summary: Put a ferry schedule in a Project and give it a standing rule. Check whether a second chat uses both.
where: Open claude.ai/projects in a browser on Mac, PC or iPad. {{fact.claude-reference-projects.availability}}

actions.title: Give the project a name
actions.do: Open Projects from the sidebar. Choose + New Project and name it Ferry Practice. If the screen asks who can see it, choose private for this exercise.
actions.see: The new project has its own page and title.
actions.stuck: If you reached your project limit, use a suitable existing practice project with space for this made-up schedule.

actions.title: Add the schedule
actions.do: Use the plus in the project knowledge area. Add text or upload a small file saying “Cove Ferry departs at 08:10. Lake Ferry departs at 09:00.”
actions.see: You can open the schedule inside the project and see both times.
actions.stuck: If the file appears only in one chat, return to the Project page and add it to the project's own knowledge.

actions.title: Set a rule
actions.do: Choose Set project instructions. Write “Use the schedule for ferry times. For an unlisted boat, say unknown.” Save the rule.
actions.see: The instruction stays with the project. A new chat in the project can use it.
actions.stuck: If the rule was sent as a message, also put it in Set project instructions.

actions.title: Try two chats
actions.do: Ask for Cove Ferry's time. Start a second chat inside Ferry Practice and ask for Bay Ferry's time. An existing chat can also be moved into a project from its chat menu. For this test, start both chats inside Ferry Practice.
actions.see: The first answer is 08:10. The second should say unknown because Bay has no entry.
actions.stuck: If the second chat cannot see the schedule, look at its project name before asking again.

roles: Study public mail help notes in one place.
Keep a team practice checklist with its rules.
Keep a game rulebook beside its design chats.

title: Make a checklist you can click
summary: An Artifact is something Claude makes that you can open and use. Build one with three boxes, then add a fourth.
where: Use Claude in a browser or its app while online. On iPad an Artifact may open on a screen of its own. Choices can vary with the template and account settings.

actions.title: Open a new chat
actions.do: Open Claude and start a fresh conversation. Look for Artifacts in the sidebar, or use the ordinary message box for this task.
actions.see: You have a place to ask for a small working object.
actions.stuck: If you only see an older Artifact, go back to a new chat before building this sample.

actions.title: Describe the checklist
actions.do: Send “Create an editable checklist Artifact titled Departure. Give it three clickable boxes called Wallet, Ticket and Charger. Let me check and clear each one.”
actions.see: A named checklist appears in an Artifact view or beside the chat.
actions.stuck: If you get an ordinary list of bullet points, ask for a working Artifact with real checkboxes.

actions.title: Click two boxes
actions.do: Check Ticket, clear Ticket and then check Wallet. Read the state of each box.
actions.see: Only Wallet ends up checked. Ticket and Charger are clear.
actions.stuck: If tapping selects text, make sure you opened the working preview instead of reading its code.

actions.title: Add a new item
actions.do: In the same chat, ask to add Glasses as the last item. Open the changed version and count its boxes.
actions.see: The checklist now has four boxes. Glasses is last and can be checked.
actions.stuck: If you only see three, look for the latest version of the Artifact and try again.

roles: Build a checklist for a fake mail change.
Make a usable form from a team checklist.
Try out a travel packing app.

title: Turn three lines of notes into a handoff
summary: Cowork can gather supplied notes into a document. Make the finished page easy for a second reader to check.
where: {{fact.claude.cowork.availability}} Use claude.ai or Claude Desktop on a Mac or PC.

actions.title: Find Cowork
actions.do: Open Claude Home. If the message box has a Chat/Cowork switch, choose Cowork. In the newer layout the same work can start in the usual message box.
actions.see: You can give the helper a job and return to that job later.
actions.stuck: If the choice is missing, check your account's access. An ordinary chat can still help you practice putting the notes in order.

actions.title: Give it the facts
actions.do: Send “Make a short handoff document from these notes. Dock test passed Monday. Sign check is waiting for the Blue team. Group finished and waiting items. Use only these notes.”
actions.see: The helper prepares a document from the small set of facts you supplied.
actions.stuck: If asked to connect mail or files, paste the two notes again. They already contain everything this job needs.

actions.title: Check the document
actions.do: Open the result. Find the finished check, the waiting check and the team linked to it. Look for an invented due date.
actions.see: Dock test belongs under finished. Sign check belongs under waiting, with Blue team. The notes give no deadline.
actions.stuck: If a made-up time appears, point back to the two source sentences and ask for a correction.

actions.title: Find it again
actions.do: Return to this same job from Claude's sidebar. Ask for an Unknowns section that lists the missing due date. Open the changed document.
actions.see: The new section makes the missing date easy to see. The two original facts still match.
actions.stuck: If you opened a different job, look for the dock-test title or the message with the two practice notes.

roles: Turn sample mail check results into a handoff.
List finished and waiting work for a team.
Put a small app's release tasks in order.
sources: Anthropic · Cowork on web, desktop and mobile

title: Read the same task on a second device
summary: Leave a tiny handoff on one device and find it on another. Pick the route your account actually offers.
where: {{fact.claude.dispatch.availability}} For Dispatch the supported desktop app must stay open on an awake computer, and the phone app needs internet.
If your account has cloud Cowork, start the job there. You can reopen it on your phone or the web without pairing a device.

actions.title: Pick a route
actions.do: Open Cowork on your desktop or phone. Choose Dispatch if the left panel offers it. Otherwise start a cloud Cowork task on Claude Home if your account has access.
actions.see: You can name the route you will use: Dispatch or a cloud Cowork task.
actions.stuck: If neither appears, do the two-line exercise on paper. Reading a note on two devices requires an eligible account.

actions.title: Set up the handoff
actions.do: Existing Dispatch users can choose Get started. Read the file access and keep-awake options and choose Finish setup when ready. Cloud users can put the sample directly into their new task.
actions.see: The task has a place for your message. The cloud route does not ask you to pair the phone for Dispatch.
actions.stuck: If you cannot find Finish setup, check which route you chose. It belongs to the Dispatch setup.

actions.title: Send two test results
actions.do: Send “Green test passed. Blue test is pending. Write a two-line handoff and put pending first.” Read the result before switching devices.
actions.see: The Blue line comes first and says pending. The Green line says passed.
actions.stuck: If both are marked complete, ask the helper to copy the two status words from your note.

actions.title: Pick it up
actions.do: On the second device, use the same account. Open the Dispatch thread or the same Cowork task and ask which test is still pending.
actions.see: It identifies Blue. You have found the same practice task again.
actions.stuck: If the handoff is missing, check the account and job name. For Dispatch, also check that the desktop is still awake and online.

roles: Read the status of a pretend mail check.
Pick up a team training note on a second screen.
Continue work on a personal app away from the desk.
sources: Anthropic · Cowork on web, desktop and mobile

title: Meet Claude Duet and test a draft
summary: Claude Duet comes from Anthropic. A dot belongs to OpenAI. Try a small Duet-style task and check the result before anything gets sent.
where: Use the public Duet example if you have no invitation. The US research preview needs an eligible personal plan and an invitation. Check the current access page when you try it.
Invited readers can follow the invitation on an iPhone or Android phone. On iPad, you can use the practice text here without signing up.

actions.title: Find the official page
actions.do: Open the Duet product link from the lesson. Look for Join the waitlist. Read which accounts and phones may join. If invited, open the invitation on the phone linked to your account.
actions.see: You can see a public sample of a Duet conversation. Eligible readers also get the signup or invitation steps.
actions.stuck: If there is no invitation, keep reading. You can do the next steps using a pencil and the sample note.

actions.title: Ask for a draft
actions.do: Give Duet this note or write a reply yourself: “Our club call moved from 2 to 3 on Monday. Draft a two-sentence reminder. Show it to me first.”
actions.see: The draft says Monday and the new time of 3. It does not invent a room, an address or a time zone.
actions.stuck: If the draft adds a time zone, ask which part of the source gave it. Have the helper remove any guess.

actions.title: Read before sending
actions.do: Find the exact text and intended reader if the tool asks to send. Your practice request was only for a draft. Stop after reading the words.
actions.see: You can complete the practice without contacting anyone. The draft is a thing you can check.
actions.stuck: If it asks for connections, keep using the sample note. A personal inbox or calendar is unnecessary here.

actions.title: Remember both names
actions.do: In the picture index, look up OpenAI dots. Compare where that lesson starts with the Claude Duet product page.
actions.see: You can point to two different products and name the company behind each one.
actions.stuck: For a Claude tool that works with files, try the separate Cowork lesson. Come back to Duet for the personal helper.

roles: Draft a reminder for a made-up mail report.
Check a practice meeting change before sending it.
Write and review a short update about an app.
sources: Anthropic · get started with Claude Duet

title: Read a public page with Claude beside it
summary: An extension adds a tool to Chrome. Open one public help page and compare Claude's answer with the words on that page.
where: Use desktop Google Chrome with an eligible Claude plan. The extension runs on a computer. Readers on iPad can follow the example in the book.
Choose a public help page for this try. Anthropic's getting-started page linked here works.

actions.title: Find the extension
actions.do: Open Anthropic’s getting-started page. Follow its Chrome Web Store link. Check that Claude comes from Anthropic. On your own or approved computer select Add to Chrome if you want it.
actions.see: Chrome shows the access the extension asks for. You can read it before deciding to install.
actions.stuck: If you see a different publisher, go back to Anthropic's link. Check local rules before installing on a work computer.

actions.title: Open the side panel
actions.do: Sign in if needed. On Chrome's toolbar, open the puzzle-piece Extensions menu and pin Claude. Select the Claude icon.
actions.see: Claude opens alongside the page. Both the article and the side panel are in the window.
actions.stuck: If you cannot see its icon, return to Extensions and find Claude in the list.

actions.title: Ask about this page
actions.do: Keep the public getting-started article open. Ask “Which desktop browser does this extension support? Find the section with the answer. Only read this page.”
actions.see: You can compare the reply with the part of the article that names Google Chrome.
actions.stuck: If the reply describes another tab, switch back to the article and give Claude its title.

actions.title: Find the line yourself
actions.do: Press Command and F on Mac or Ctrl and F on Windows. Search for Chrome. Read the sentence around the word. Then close the Claude panel.
actions.see: You have checked the original page and finished the task without asking the extension to fill forms or follow links.
actions.stuck: If the search finds too many matches, search for a longer phrase from the reply or look under the setup heading.

roles: Read a public mail guide and check its summary.
Find a requirement in a public team app guide.
Check whether your app help matches its instructions.
sources: Anthropic · get started with Claude in Chrome
